comparison: Perfect agreement on C30-C36. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the ER characterization findings through meiotic phases. OpenEval notes adequate sample sizes (n=5-9) for descriptive observations; peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of 'solid evidence' and 'basic characterization' that will be relied upon by the community.

Perfect agreement on C39-C46. Both evaluations support the spatial organization findings showing paternal mitochondria exclusion from maternal organelles. OpenEval highlights adequate sample sizes (n=5-34) and dynamic evidence from cytoplasmic streaming; peer reviewers accept these observations without challenge.

Partial agreement on C47-C50. OpenEval supports these kca-1(RNAi) findings showing organelle packing independence (C47-C50) but rates C51-C52 as UNCERTAIN due to small sample size (n=4) for evolutionary conservation claims. Peer review R3 groups all claims (C47-C52) together as SUPPORTED without distinguishing the conservation claim weakness.

OpenEval R4 addresses only C51-C52 (evolutionary conservation in C. macrosperma) and rates as UNCERTAIN due to very small sample size (n=4). Peer review R3 includes these claims within a broader group (C47-C52) rated as SUPPORTED, not separately evaluating the conservation claim's limitations.

Perfect agreement on C53-C62. Both evaluations support the differential ER penetration findings. OpenEval emphasizes time-resolved imaging data (n=7-10) and temporal resolution; peer reviewers acknowledge this characterization showing ER penetration while other maternal organelles are excluded.

Perfect agreement on C64-C66. Both evaluations support the BAF-1 permeability findings. OpenEval notes reasonable inference about ER envelope not forming complete barrier; peer reviewers implicitly accept these mechanistic observations as part of overall 'solid evidence.'

Strong agreement on C3, C70-C74, C78 regarding mei-1(RNAi) effects on microtubule-severing and sperm movement. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes large sample sizes (n=51 total) and quantitative measurements; peer reviewers accept these findings as identifying proteins critical for limiting cytoplasmic streaming. OpenEval R7 also includes C5, C76-C77 not in peer R6.

Partial overlap on C76-C77, C80. OpenEval R7 includes klp-7(RNAi) data (C76-C77) within broader SUPPORTED evaluation of microtubule effects. Peer R7 separately addresses these klp-7 observations as SUPPORTED, noting low capture frequency contrasts with mei-1 and sets up double depletion rationale.

Minimal overlap on C80 only. OpenEval R8 rates C79-C80 as SUPPORTED, acknowledging limitations in interpreting capture event consequences. Peer R7 includes C80 within klp-7 observations rated as SUPPORTED, focusing on low capture frequency.

Agreement on C4, C90-C92 regarding ATX-2 effects on sperm content cohesion. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes three independent depletion methods strengthening conclusions; peer reviewers accept the scattering phenotype and identify ATX-2 as critical for maintaining paternal organelle grouping.

Significant disagreement on C6, C93-C103 regarding double depletion experiments. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting statistical support (p=0.011) and acknowledging low single mutant sample sizes but stating data 'qualitatively support' synergistic effect. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of significant difference between single and double knockdowns, low sample sizes (n=15-24), and stating 'strength of conclusion would be greatly improved' with additional data.

Partial overlap on C99-C101 (ATX-2 single depletion). OpenEval R11 includes these within broader SUPPORTED evaluation of double depletion synergy. Peer R10 rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these single depletion results are part of concern about low sample sizes (n=15) preventing statistical significance and limiting confidence in negative findings.

Disagreement on C7-C8 (main conclusions about both mechanisms working together). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing these as appropriate synthesis of katanin/kinesin-13 and ATX-2 results with double depletion showing synergistic effects. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating conclusion is weakened by concerns about double depletion experiments and lack of strong statistical support between single and double mutants.

OpenEval R9 addresses C81-C84 (correlating ER morphology with sperm movement patterns) and rates as SUPPORTED, noting correlative rather than causative relationship. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval R13 addresses C104-C108 (speculative hypotheses about viscosity and active processes for ER penetration) and rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable hypotheses for future investigation but remain unproven. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R14 addresses C109-C111 (speculative claims about capture mechanisms and ER envelope persistence) and rates as UNCERTAIN, noting mechanistic connections remain speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R15 addresses C122-C125 (control observations and summary of differential depletion effects) and rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate synthesis of experimental observations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R16 addresses C126-C129 (spindle positioning and microtubule bundle observations) and rates as SUPPORTED, noting sound reasoning though partly speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R17 addresses C130-C135 (synthesis with prior literature including mouse studies and C. elegans work) and rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate contextualization within existing knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R18 addresses C136-C137 (volume calculations and capture probability) and rates as SUPPORTED, noting correct mathematics though biological significance is speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R19 addresses C138-C139 (negative results on capture consequences and comparison to mouse studies) and rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
